title: Reframing the End of School Countdown
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave shares a message that Dr. John Tanner, a middle-school principal he'd been coaching, sent to his own faculty about how to communicate end-of-year countdowns. Tanner argues that while countdown excitement is natural and worth celebrating, leaders should frame it around a goal to accomplish in the time remaining rather than just the finish line itself, and should stay sensitive to students for whom school is a source of stability they'll miss over summer. The piece doubles as a case study in how Dave's coaching ideas propagate into a real school's language and practice.
points: Reframes the ubiquitous "X days left" countdown from a pure finish-line marker into a challenge to use remaining time purposefully, with concrete phrasing examples ("22 days left to give everything you've got as a ___ grader").

Cautions that summer isn't uniformly exciting for all students — some experience their most stable, structured time at school and will genuinely miss it — so celebratory messaging needs a companion note of care.
Suggests pairing the reframed countdown with concrete summer goal-setting and connection-planning for students, not just marking days off a calendar.
Demonstrates a coaching-to-practice pipeline: an idea Dave shared in office hours with a school's staff became a principal's own faculty-wide communication.
quotes: Most of us have some type of countdown going on in our heads as we inch closer and closer to the finish line of the marathon that is a school year.
In our office hours last week with Dave Stuart, he encouraged us to frame the countdown in a way that challenges our students (and ourselves) to make the most of the time remaining.

We also want to be careful of how we communicate our excitement because not all of our students are looking forward to summer. For many of our students, some of their happiest, safest, and most structured time is right here with us.
Our ask: If you're publicizing a countdown, please frame it in a way that connects to a goal to accomplish (beyond just finishing) and/or a feeling to have.
It's a countdown with a purpose. We still have more than 10% of the year remaining. Let's optimize it.
